dicas.texto: Para transformar uma fração em porcentagem, o denominador deve ser 100. Se você tem 4000 e quer chegar em 100, que operação reduz esse valor?
Pense na relação entre 4000 e 100. Quantas vezes o 100 cabe dentro do 4000? Divida 4000 por 100 para descobrir o fator de escala.
Você está quase lá! Se você cortar dois zeros do 4000, qual número sobra? Esse é o seu fator de escala.
O fator de escala é 40. Agora, aplique a mesma divisão (÷ 40) tanto no denominador quanto no numerador (8 ÷ 40) para encontrar a porcentagem.
Lembre-se: porcentagem é uma razão com denominador 100. Como você pode ajustar 4000 para 100?
Use o mesmo fator de escala que você descobriu no passo anterior para manter a proporção.
Divida 5000 pelo mesmo fator de escala que você usou para o 4000.
Calcule 5000 ÷ 40. O resultado será o numerador sobre 100, indicando a porcentagem final.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado com as partes da tarefa e, abaixo, uma TABELA de razões com três linhas — Total, Part 1 e Part 2 — e, em cada linha, quatro grupos de células: (1) a razão ORIGINAL (numerador e denominador, dois campos); (2) a coluna "Operation": dois seletores em que o aluno escolhe × ou ÷ (um para o numerador, um para o denominador); (3) a coluna "Scale Factor": dois campos com o fator aplicado ao numerador e ao denominador; (4) o RESULTADO: um campo para o numerador da razão equivalente, cujo denominador já vem impresso como 100 (isto é, a porcentagem), e um campo para o valor da porcentagem. Botão Hint; botão Done. Cada célula preenchida é um passo do aluno; a tabela inteira tem 24 células a completar.

dicas.texto: For each ratio, identify the quantity in the numerator and the original total in the denominator.
Enter the whole amount over the original amount for Total, the chipped amount over the original amount for Part 1, and the new total over the original amount for Part 2.
Use 4000 as the original total in every denominator, and use 4000, 8, and 5000 as the three numerators.
Complete the rows by entering the whole-to-whole ratio, the chipped-to-original ratio, and the new-total-to-original ratio in that order.
Ask whether the denominator must become smaller or larger when changing 4000 into 100.
Compare the original denominator with 100, then choose the operation that changes 4000 into 100.
The denominator is reduced from 4000 to 100, so select division and use the same factor in both positions.
Choose the division symbol and the factor that makes 4000 become 100, then apply that same choice to the numerator.
Equivalent ratios keep the same relationship when both parts are divided by the same factor.
Divide the Part 1 numerator by the scale factor, and place the result over the printed denominator 100.
Use the calculation 8 divided by 40 for the new numerator, then use that same value as the percentage.
Perform the final division of 8 by 40, enter that result in the equivalent-ratio numerator, and repeat it in the percentage field.
Focus on the relationship between the original denominator and the percentage denominator of 100.
Find the factor that changes 4000 into 100, then use the same operation and factor for the numerator.
Because 4000 is being reduced to 100, the operation is division rather than multiplication.
Select the division symbol and the factor obtained by dividing 4000 by 100, then repeat that choice for both positions.
The new floor requires more sticks than the original model, so the percentage can be greater than the whole amount.
Divide the Part 2 numerator by the selected scale factor, then enter the result in both percentage-result fields.
Use 5000 divided by 40 for the equivalent numerator and keep the printed denominator at 100.
Carry out the final division of 5000 by 40, enter that value as the numerator over 100, and repeat it as the percentage.
The original total represents the entire starting amount, so its percentage must describe the whole.
Use the same division by the scale factor in the Total row, then express the equivalent ratio over 100.
Both Total-row operations are division, both scale factors are 40, and the result must have denominator 100.
Divide the Total numerator and denominator by 40, enter the resulting numerator in both Total result fields, and then press Done.

exercicio.statement:
Malila is building a model house out of 4000 craft sticks.

Part 1)If 8 of the sticks have a chip in them and cannot be used, what percentage of the craft sticks are chipped?

Part 2) If she decides to add another floor, requiring 5000 sticks in total, what percentage of the original amount of sticks is needed? Part 1)If 8 of the sticks have a chip in them and cannot be used, what percentage of the craft sticks are chipped?
Part 2) If she decides to add another floor, requiring 5000 sticks in total, what percentage of the original amount of sticks is needed?
